I have farmed in Quzhou for over forty years. I am fifty-five now and I never went to school, but I know my land. I have about eight mu of good flat land that I can irrigate from the well. Every year I do the same thing because it works: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what the land here is for.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I use Jimai 22, an improved variety I buy from the seed shop. It gives steady yields. Before sowing I do rotary tillage to make the soil fine. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer as base and then topdress with urea when the wheat turns green and at jointing. The wheat needs water, so I will irrigate four times: the winter storage irrigation, then at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I also spray four times total—herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once because the spring gets damp. If the weather is normal I expect about 500 kg per mu.

Right after I harvest the wheat in early June, I plant maize. I use Denghai 605, a hybrid seed. It grows fast and strong. I do not till for the maize; I plant directly into the wheat stubble to save time and moisture. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and that is usually enough. I irrigate twice, at the big trumpet stage and grain filling. I spray about three times for weeds and insects. The maize should give me about 550 kg per mu.

This is what I do every year. It feeds my household and gives me grain to sell.
